chunks.text: SPI General Ledger (GL) Module — ENQUIRIES Source: Sidat Hyder Financials Software Guide ### Enquiries [Transactions:]{.underline} This is a comprehensive on-screen search facility that filters and then accordingly displays GL transactions as per various criteria that is defined by the user. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Enquiries menu and then select Transactions. Selecting the options displays a list of all transactions that are present in the database. These transactions can now be filtered according to various criteria that are made available to the user in order to flush out, for display purposes, those transactions that are being searched for. Simply click the *Filer* button, which will take you to the criteria definition screen. Using the available options on the screen will facilitate you to track down transactions you may wish to see. The criteria screen contains: - A list of column names corresponding to voucher fields - Standard buttons representing criteria such as \>(greater than), \<(less than), = (equal to) etc. - In addition the screen also contains a list of standard functions that may

fields - Standard buttons representing criteria such as \>(greater than), \<(less than), = (equal to) etc. - In addition the screen also contains a list of standard functions that may be manipulated to generate the desired results. Use the above facilities to generate the required data. For example if you wish to see transactions which have a Debit amount of 5,625 then commit the following query via the *Filter* screen Debit \> 5625 The above lists transactions meeting the criteria. You can also directly type in a specific query in the *Specify filter* window or you may click on the various buttons (fields, criteria, functions) available on the screen and each click types in the required characters in the *Specify Filter* window to build up the eventual query. [Account Summary]{.underline} As the title implies, this options displays a summary of transactions for any given account. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Enquiries menu and then select *Account Summary*. Click the Next and Previous buttons to view corresponding accounts. If multi currency is being used then choose the required Currency from the available drop down list box. Specify whether you want the summary to reflect posted, un-posted or both type of transactions. Based on the above a summary is generated containing the following columns: - Account Code - Account Title - Period of the Account - Debit and Credit of Opening Balance, Activity and Closing Balance [Summary of balances:]{.underline} This option displays a summary of all accounts and these balances are shown for the selected currency. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Enquiries menu and then select Summary of balances. Based on the above a summary is generated containing the following columns: - Account Code - Account Title - Debit - Credit - Balance [Activity Log:]{.underline} This is a comprehensive enquiries facility, which may be used by GL users to track the various processes that are performed, by various users, on the GL database. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Enquiries menu and then select *Activity Log*. The activity log screen contains various criteria that may be manipulated to generate results from the database based on the query defined through this criterion. Proper manipulation of the various available criteria includes the filtration of data to make available listings such - User wise activities, including log in and log out times - The various activities that

the various available criteria includes the filtration of data to make available listings such - User wise activities, including log in and log out times - The various activities that have been performed by various or specific users on a particular voucher - Activities performed on a particular date by a particular user on a particular voucher or voucher type - A specific type of activity by all users or a specific user within a particular period - All activities within a given period for a particular company (if multi companies are being used) - Etc. The above were examples. Now simply go the screen and start listings according to your requirements. ### Frequently Asked Questions (Additional Test Coverage) Q: How do I filter and search GL transactions on screen? A: Go to Enquiries > Transactions, click Filter, and build a query using column names, criteria buttons (greater than, less than, equal to), and standard functions — e.g. 'Debit > 5625'. Q: How do I see a summary of transactions for one account? A: Go to Enquiries > Account Summary,

than, equal to), and standard functions — e.g. 'Debit > 5625'. Q: How do I see a summary of transactions for one account? A: Go to Enquiries > Account Summary, choose the ledger account code, and specify whether to include posted, un-posted, or both types of transactions. Q: How do I see balances across all accounts at once? A: Go to Enquiries > Summary of balances — shows Account Code, Title, Debit, Credit, and Balance for the selected currency. Q: How can I track which user performed an action on a voucher? A: Use Enquiries > Activity Log — it can filter by user, activity type, date, specific voucher or voucher type, and login/logout times.

SPI General Ledger (GL) Module — PROCESS Source: Sidat Hyder Financials Software Guide ### Process [Vouchers Verification:]{.underline} As the name of the option implies this option is used to verify or un-verify all entered vouchers before they are actually posted. Posting in the GL system basically refers to the concepts that after posting these vouchers are locked for any further process and cannot be un-posted. However, verified vouchers can be unverified though a verified voucher is functionally the same as a posted voucher except that it can be unlocked/unverified as opposed to a posted voucher, which is not reversible once the process has been applied. [Getting there;]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Verification. [Posting:]{.underline} The posting option basically locks the records for which posting is being run and updates posted balances while locking the posted voucher from undergoing any further modifications. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Posting. This displays a list of all voucher types and corresponding vouchers that have been entered.

there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Posting. This displays a list of all voucher types and corresponding vouchers that have been entered. The user is provided the facility to select one or more than one vouchers for posting. Select *All voucher Types* to simultaneously post all vouchers. [Period End]{.underline} As the name of the option implies this option is provided to enable the user to close periods that fall within the financial year of the company. Please note that once the period has been closed no vouchers entered during that period may be modified or deleted. Similarly, any entry for the period is not allowed though you can view/take out reports for all entered transactions for the period. Before you close the period, make sure that you have posted all the vouchers that were entered during the period. If you have marked any voucher for auto-reversal at close of period then the period end process creates a new voucher for the reversal effect and which is visible in the next period. +---+---+-----------------------------------------------------------------+

Functionally both options perform the same basics and the only difference between the two lies in the fact that corresponding to titles, the permanent year end may be run only once to finally close the year whereas the temporary year end option remains available to be run as many times as required until and unless the permanent year end has been run to close the fiscal year. run as many times as required until and unless the permanent year end has been run to close the fiscal year. The year-end processes (both) initialize the income & expense accounts making them available for fresh entries for the year that follows. All document numbers are initialized as the system adapts the new year. As mentioned above, the permanent year-end can be run only once, after which the user is not allowed to modify data pertaining to that year whereas the temporary year-end process may be run multiple times to build fresh balances reflecting transaction entered between these processes of running the temporary year end. The system provides the user to create or not to create the year-end vouchers. If you have marked any voucher for auto-reversal at close of year then the year-end process creates a new voucher for the reversal effect and which is visible in the first period of the falling year. +---+---+-----------------------------------------------------------------+ | | * | > Please make sure to take a backup of all data before running | | | * | > year-end

[Import Voucher:]{.underline} As the title implies this utility is provided to the GL user if the user wishes to import vouchers that have been generated through other applications, into the SHMA GL. If the facility is required to be used, we request the user to consult our technical staff for assistance. [Foreign Currency Gain/Loss:]{.underline} This option is used to calculate gain or loss that result via fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rate effecting foreign currency transactions recorded in the GL. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Foreign Currency Gain/Loss. This option may be run at any time of the year and the results may be viewed in all/any reporting currencies/currency. Please note that the system will calculate Foreign Currency Gain/Loss for only those accounts which have been defined as 'Asset or Liability' type account and the option to calculate F.C. Translation has been checked in the COA setup. Foreign currency gain/loss is computed based on the exchange rate (of the particular date of the

and the option to calculate F.C. Translation has been checked in the COA setup. Foreign currency gain/loss is computed based on the exchange rate (of the particular date of the transaction) that have been entered by the user. Obviously, this exchange rate needs to be different than the one entered in the voucher. The 'Calculate' button displays a calculation sheet, which demonstrates the gain/loss calculation. A calculation results in an accumulated balance of already created F.C. Gain/Loss vouchers that are displayed under the column titled, 'F.C. Gain/Loss already calculated'. A 'Generate Voucher' option is provided that generates a gain/loss voucher based on the above calculation. Click the button to initiate the process after selecting the type of voucher that you want to create to record the gain/loss. You must provide the number of the voucher if it has not been marked as to be auto-generated. Please note that these generated vouchers are automatically posted during the creation process and thus are unavailable for editing. However, these may be deleted by using the 'Delete' option. A list of generated voucher(s) is displayed and the user can simply select and delete the required voucher(s). [Re-Calculate Reporting Currencies:]{.underline} As the title implies, use this option to re-calculate reporting currencies that are reflects as such in various reports/online screen queries. [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Re-Calculate Reporting Currencies. The user may use this option any time, however it is best served in two occasions. **Case 1**: The change in the number of the reporting currency, which at times results with and at times without the introduction of a new reporting currency. This would require a re-calculation of reporting currencies. **Case 2**: The exchange rate of an existing reporting currency is modified and you wish to recalculate existing transactions for the currency to reflect the fresh rate. Click the option to open a selection window and specify the criteria for recalculating the data. Click the

to recalculate existing transactions for the currency to reflect the fresh rate. Click the option to open a selection window and specify the criteria for recalculating the data. Click the Re-Calculate button to see the requested results. [Replace activity accounts:]{.underline} The old accounts can be replaced by the new ones. On the main menu go to Process and click on the replace activity accounts. A screen will be displayed which allows you to enter old a/c number, new a/c number, voucher type and date. [Replace project code:]{.underline} Similarly, project code can also be replaced by entering the following options: [Replace analysis 2 code:]{.underline} Analysis 2 can be replaced by the new analysis 2. [Data Transfer:]{.underline} This utility is provided for the benefit of those users who use the GL package by running it on multiple sites while at the same time wishing to produce consolidated reports. Using this facility data from all sites can be merged independent of database type(s). [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Data Transfer. from all sites can be merged independent of database type(s). [Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Process menu and then select Data Transfer. The option simply merges data of multiple sites into one central database. The sites are treated as the source databases whereas the central db is treated as the target database in which data needs to be consolidated. Please ensure that identical installation parameters are defined at all sites for which data needs to be merged. Contact our support staff to facilitate the same. The following options are available under the data transfer option: [Export Data:]{.underline} Clicking the *Export Data* option opens up a window that contains various criteria that may be manipulatively defined for the export process. Data for a specific range of periods, specific sites and specific dates may also be transferred after making relative selections available on the screen. We suggest that you contact our support staff to initially configure the data transfer mode, which may be both online, or offline. An offline data transfer may take place by simply compressing

that you contact our support staff to initially configure the data transfer mode, which may be both online, or offline. An offline data transfer may take place by simply compressing (through choosing the "Make Zip File" option) and emailing it to the relevant site. The email process is also automated by recording the email address of the target site into the site setup defined earlier. [Import Data:]{.underline} This option is used to import data from one site to another. Prior to running the option, the user is warned that existing data will be overwritten. On receiving a go-ahead signal from the user (in the form of a *yes* click) the standard file dialogue box appears showing the file containing the data that needs to be exported. Selecting the required file and choosing to proceed starts the process and prompts the user on successful completion. ### Frequently Asked Questions (Additional Test Coverage) Q: What's the difference between a verified voucher and a posted voucher? A: A verified voucher is functionally the same as a posted one, except it can still be

Coverage) Q: What's the difference between a verified voucher and a posted voucher? A: A verified voucher is functionally the same as a posted one, except it can still be unlocked/unverified — a posted voucher cannot be un-posted once the process has been applied. Q: What happens when a period is closed? A: No vouchers entered during that period may be modified, deleted, or added, though reports can still be viewed — all vouchers should be posted before closing the period. Q: What's the difference between permanent and temporary Year End? A: Permanent Year End can be run only once to finally close the fiscal year, after which data for that year can't be modified. Temporary Year End can be run multiple times to build fresh balances before the permanent close. Q: How is Foreign Currency Gain/Loss calculated? A: Based on the exchange rate of the transaction date entered by the user, but only for accounts defined as Asset or Liability type with F.C. Translation checked in the Chart of Accounts setup. the user, but only for accounts defined as Asset or Liability type with F.C. Translation checked in the Chart of Accounts setup. Q: Can an import of vouchers from another application be done directly? A: Yes, via Process > Import Voucher, but the data must be formatted for SPI's specific temporary import tables — technical staff assistance is recommended.

[Getting there:]{.underline} On the main menu screen go to the Reports menu and then select *Chart of Accounts*. Click the option that takes you to the printing screen. There are various criteria available that allow you to print the Chart of Accounts for the given range of account codes. You may sort the report on account code, title creation date etc. If required, apply various available filters to generate the report based on required criteria. [Transaction Listing:]{.underline} As the title implies, the selected report displays a summary of transactions for any given account. The generated list may contain all vouchers for the above specification or a range of vouchers falling within a certain period or between two given periods You can also specify a listing of these vouchers based on being entered between a specific range of dates or even modified between a specific range of dates irrespective of entry dates. As you will see on the screen you are also allowed to list these vouchers in various reporting currencies (if the multi currency option has been enabled) which means you can generate a listing of these vouchers entered in currency A but reported in currency B with appropriate reflection of conversion rates. A: Go to Reports > Chart of Accounts, then apply filters and sort by account code, title, or creation date as needed. Q: How do I generate a list of transactions for a specific voucher type? A: Go to Reports > Transaction Listing — can be filtered by voucher type, period or date range, and printed in any reporting currency if multi-currency is enabled. Q: What does the Trial Balance report offer? A: One of the most useful reporting features in GL — besides multiple filter criteria, it has a drill-down feature allowing you to trace transactions right down to the individual voucher entry. Q: How do I drill down from a Trial Balance to the actual voucher? A: Double-click any account code on the report

transactions right down to the individual voucher entry. Q: How do I drill down from a Trial Balance to the actual voucher? A: Double-click any account code on the report to view its Ledger, then click again to reach the voucher level. Q: What does the Age Analysis report show? A: A summary or detailed breakdown of Receivables, Payables, or all Open Items, broken into up to five custom periods, with optional minimum/maximum amount filters. Q: What does the Budget Report show? A: A budget variance report — variance is calculated only between the last two selected columns in the 'Select Report' group, for a chosen account range, cost centre, or period range.

SPI Support Knowledge Base — Inventory & Sync Incidents INCIDENT TYPE: Stock Count Mismatch Between Warehouses Symptoms: A client reports that the same item shows different stock quantities on two different screens (e.g., Stock Status Report vs. Warehouse Transfer screen). Root Cause (most common): An in-transit stock transfer between warehouses was left in "Pending Receipt" status and never confirmed at the destination warehouse. The source warehouse has already deducted the stock, but the destination hasn't received it yet, so the item appears to be "missing" from both counts temporarily. Resolution Steps: 1. Check Inventory > Transfers > Pending Receipts for any transfer involving the affected item. 2. If a transfer is stuck in Pending, confirm with the warehouse staff whether the physical stock actually arrived. 3. If it arrived, complete the receipt confirmation in SPI. If it did not arrive, escalate to warehouse operations — this is a physical logistics issue, not a software bug. Escalate to Engineering only if: no pending transfer exists and the mismatch still cannot be explained by manual stock adjustments. INCIDENT TYPE: Reorder Point Not

issue, not a software bug. Escalate to Engineering only if: no pending transfer exists and the mismatch still cannot be explained by manual stock adjustments. INCIDENT TYPE: Reorder Point Not Triggering Purchase Suggestion Symptoms: Stock has fallen below the configured reorder point, but no suggested Purchase Order appears in Purchase > Suggested Orders. Root Cause (most common): The item's Replenishment Rule was configured with a "Preferred Supplier" left blank. SPI will not auto-generate a suggested PO without a preferred supplier assigned, even if the reorder point logic is otherwise correctly configured. Resolution Steps: 1. Navigate to Inventory > Configuration > Replenishment Rules for the affected item. 2. Confirm a Preferred Supplier is assigned. 3. If missing, assign one and re-run the nightly Reorder Suggestion job manually via Inventory > Utilities > Run Reorder Job Now. Escalate to Engineering only if: a preferred supplier is assigned and the item still doesn't generate a suggestion after a manual job run. generate a suggestion after a manual job run. INCIDENT TYPE: Barcode Scan Not Recognized During Stock Count Symptoms: Warehouse staff scan a barcode during a cycle count and get "Item Not Found," even though the item exists in the system. Root Cause (most common): The barcode printed on the physical label doesn't match the Bin Location code format configured in SPI (see Implementation Guide — Bin Location codes must follow AA-00-00 format). Older labels printed before a warehouse reconfiguration are a frequent cause of this after a client's warehouse layout changes. Resolution Steps: 1. Confirm the current Bin Location format under Inventory > Configuration > Warehouse Setup. 2. Compare against the physical label — if it doesn't match, the label needs to be reprinted, this is not a data or software issue. Escalate to Engineering only if: the label format matches the configured Bin Location format exactly and the scan still fails. ### Frequently Asked Questions (Additional Test Coverage) Q: Why does the same item show different stock on the Stock Status Report versus the Warehouse Transfer screen?
